text: RESULTS: Imaging: Ultrasound of the Neck shows a well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the updated findings; the ultrasound suggests a cystic nature, yet the physical exam describes a firm nodule where the overlying skin cannot be pinched. Given the skin involvement and the history of colon cancer, I need to rule out an epidermal inclusion cyst versus a cutaneous metastasis. Does the skin over the nodule show any signs of redness, warmth, or a visible punctum?

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of redness, warmth, or a visible punctum makes an inflamed epidermal cyst less likely, especially given the skin cannot be pinched and your history of colon cancer. To definitively distinguish between a benign cyst and a cutaneous metastasis, I must proceed with the previously ordered histology. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Metastasis from Colon Cancer.
